translation: When it moves, one suffers lower abdominal pain rushing up to the heart, with u瘕u (abdominal masses), hernia, and enuresis, fullness and vexation of the flanks, and in women, loss of the ability to conceive. It also says: When cun and chi are both firm, going straight up and straight down, this is the Chong vessel, with cold hernia in the chest. Zhang Zhongjing said: In cold damage, when the moving qi is on the right, one must not cause sweating; if one sweats it, there will be nosebleed and thirst, vexation of the heart, and vomiting immediately upon drinking water; (first use Wuling San, then Zhuye Tang) one must not purge; if one purges it, the fluids will be exhausted internally, with dizziness, dry throat, dry nose, and palpitations.
